meta.title: Neurons guide
meta.description: How to install and use Neurons, the live view of what Claude Code does in a repository, with answers to common questions.
lang.label: Language
hero.title: See what Claude Code does in your repo, while it does it
hero.lead: Neurons is a command, neu, that opens a page in your browser with your repository drawn as a network. Every file and folder is a node. When Claude Code reads, searches, edits, creates or deletes something, a light travels to that file in the color of the action.
hero.lead2: Use it to watch how the agent works: what it reads first, how much it explores before it edits, which instructions load on their own and what its subagents get up to. It runs on your machine and only looks at paths, never at what your files contain.
hero.imgAlt: Neurons showing its own repository as a glowing network, with reads in cyan, an edit in amber and the activity panel on the right
hero.caption: The viewer on Neurons' own repository. Cyan lines are reads, amber is an edit, the repo sits in the center and files outside it (your ~/.claude) form their own cluster on the left. The floating stream at the bottom left says what Claude is doing now; the panel on the right has the counters, the tools used and every action.
hero.req: You need Node 22.12 or later, git and Claude Code. Tested with Claude Code 2.1.285 and 2.1.288 on macOS.
ai.title: Set it up with your AI
ai.lead: Open Claude Code in any folder and paste this prompt. First replace <repo-url> with the address you got Neurons from, either a Git URL or a folder on your disk. Claude clones it into ~/neurons, builds it, links the neu command and checks that it runs.
ai.prompt:
Install the Neurons CLI (npm package neurons-cli) on this machine. Do these steps in order and stop to tell me if one fails.

1. Run `node --version`. Neurons needs Node 22.12 or later. If mine is older, stop and tell me how to update it; do not change my Node install yourself.
2. Clone the repository: `git clone <repo-url> ~/neurons`. If <repo-url> is still a placeholder, ask me for it. If ~/neurons already exists, ask me before touching it.
3. In ~/neurons run `npm install` and then `npm run build`. The build must leave a file at ~/neurons/dist/cli.mjs.
4. In ~/neurons run `npm link`. It puts two global commands on my PATH, `neu` and `neurons`, which are the same program. If it fails with EEXIST because another package already owns `neu`, tell me which package it is and do not use --force without asking. If it fails with EACCES, explain my options instead of using sudo.
5. Check the install: `neu --version` must print a version, and `neu doctor` must run. Show me what doctor reports. A note that the hooks are not installed is expected at this point.
6. Tell me in two lines how to use it: cd into any repository and run `neu`, then open Claude Code in that same repository.

If I want the command to have another name, the names come from the "bin" field in ~/neurons/package.json. Changing a key there (for example "neu" to "nr") and running `npm unlink -g neurons-cli` and then `npm link` again does it. Ask me whether I want that before you change anything.
ai.note: The prompt makes Claude stop and ask before it touches an existing ~/neurons folder or forces the link over another package's neu.
manual.title: Set it up by hand
manual.s1.title: Clone and build
manual.s1.body: npm run build builds the web page, the CLI and this guide into dist/.
manual.s2.title: Link the command
manual.s2.body: This puts neu and neurons on your PATH (they are the same program), pointing at ~/neurons/dist/cli.mjs. To remove them later, run npm unlink -g neurons-cli. If npm link fails with EACCES, your global npm folder belongs to root; a Node version manager such as nvm or fnm avoids that without sudo.
manual.s3.title: Check it
manual.s3.body: neu --version prints the version. neu doctor checks Node, the hooks, the Claude Code settings files and whether the page is built.
manual.s4.title: Pick another name (optional)
manual.s4.body: The command names come from "bin" in ~/neurons/package.json. Change a key, for example neu to nr, then unlink and link again. The help text and the messages keep saying neu.
use.title: Use it
use.s1.title: Start the viewer in your repo
use.s1.body: The browser opens at http://127.0.0.1:7777 (or the next free port). From a subfolder, neu moves up to the root of the git repository and tells you. You can also pass the folder: neu ~/projects/api.
use.s2.title: Open Claude Code in that repo
use.s2.body: In another terminal, the way you always do. A session that was already open picks up the hooks without a restart. The network lights up with every action.
use.s3.title: Close it
use.s3.body: Press Ctrl+C in the terminal where neu runs, or run neu stop from any other one. The hooks come out and your settings go back to how they were, byte for byte.
use.more: While the viewer runs, this guide is also at /help and the architecture page at /architecture on the same address. neu help lists every command and option.
faq.title: Questions
faq.lead: Grouped by theme. Each question has its own link, so you can send someone straight to an answer.
faq.what.a:
A live map of what Claude Code does inside one repository. Your repo becomes a network of files and folders, and each action the agent takes (a read, a search, an edit, a new file, a deletion, a command) shows up as a light on the file it touched. A side panel lists the same actions with their details, and a timeline shows them in order.

It is meant for watching and learning: how the agent explores a codebase, how many files it reads before changing one, which CLAUDE.md files and rules it loads, and what its subagents do.
faq.cli.a:
Yes. You run neu in a terminal. It starts a small server on 127.0.0.1, tells Claude Code to send its events there while it runs, and opens the page in your browser. There is no account and no cloud service, and nothing leaves your machine.

neurons is the same command with a longer name.
faq.install.a: Neurons is not on npm yet, so you install it from its repository: clone, npm install, npm run build and npm link. You can let Claude do it with a prompt or type the steps yourself. You need Node 22.12 or later.
faq.other-repo.q: How do I use it in another repo?
faq.other-repo.a:
Go to that repo and run neu, or pass the path from anywhere: neu ~/projects/api. Nothing needs installing per repo. neu writes its hooks into that repo when it starts and takes them out when it closes.

Each repo gets its own viewer on its own port, so you can watch several at once. See several repos.
faq.nodes.q: What are the nodes and the lines?
faq.nodes.a:
Every file and every folder is a node. The lines join each item to the folder it lives in, so the network is your folder tree, with the repository root as the big node in the middle. When something happens, the light travels from the root down those lines to the file.

Files outside the repo that Claude touches, such as your skills in ~/.claude or something in /tmp, gather in a separate cluster. The files touched most keep a soft glow, like a heat map. In repos with more than 1,500 nodes, folders start collapsed and open on their own when Claude goes into them; you can also click a collapsed folder to open it.
faq.colors.a:
The color is the kind of action. A faint pulse means Claude decided to use a tool; the full pulse means the tool finished.

ColorActionWhat triggers it
cyanreadClaude reads a file
bluesearchgrep, rg, find, Glob or Grep; the files found flash faintly
amberedita change to an existing file
greencreatea new file or folder
reddeletea file or folder removed
pinkmovemv or git mv
violetcontextinstructions that load on their own: CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules
whitecommandany other Bash command
orangeskillClaude uses a skill. A skill is not a file in your repo, so it shows in the feed, the Tools counters and the Timeline
tealMCPa call to an MCP server tool; it lights a file when the call names one
slatetoolother Claude tools, such as Agent or WebFetch
yellowsubagenta subagent starts or ends
gray, blinkingfailurea tool call that failed
dim grayexternal changesomething changed on disk outside Claude (your editor, another terminal)

The Legend at the bottom of the panel shows the same list inside the app.
faq.disconnected.q: Why do I see one dot and "Disconnected"?
faq.disconnected.a:
"Disconnected" means the page cannot reach its viewer. The tree arrives over that connection, so without it the network stays empty; the dot next to the Neurons name at the top is the logo. Most of the time the viewer behind that tab is no longer running. It was closed with Ctrl+C or neu stop, it crashed, or it started again on another port. It also happens when the page comes from somewhere other than the viewer, such as a Vite dev server started without NEURONS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

Run neu ls to see which viewers run and at which address. Start neu again in that repo: if it gets the same port, the open tab reconnects by itself, and if not, neu open opens the right address.

A single node with "Connected" is a different case: the viewer runs on a folder with nothing in its tree, usually an empty folder or the wrong one. The repo name next to the logo tells you which folder it is watching.
faq.subagents.q: How do I tell subagents and sessions apart?
faq.subagents.a:
Each subagent puts a colored ring of its own around the nodes it touches, and its rows in the feed name the agent type. The Agent filter in the panel lists every subagent so you can isolate one. A subagent that works in an isolated worktree shows up on the matching files of your main repo, with a worktree tag on its rows.

Sessions get a softer treatment. With two or more active sessions in the same repo, each one gets its own muted hue: a thin ring on the nodes it touches, a border on its feed rows and a chip in the Sessions line that filters by it. A session counts as active until it ends, or for 10 minutes after its last event. A /clear does not start a separate session in this sense. With a single session the view stays plain.
faq.restart.q: Do I need to restart Claude Code?
faq.restart.a:
No. A session that is already open picks up the hooks as soon as neu starts, and lets go of them when it stops, without any hook error. This was checked with Claude Code 2.1.288 in real interactive sessions. When it starts, neu lists the Claude Code sessions it finds open in the repo, with their process IDs.

With an older Claude Code, if a session shows no events, leave it with /exit and come back with claude --continue.
faq.several-sessions.q: Can I watch several sessions in the same repo?
faq.several-sessions.a: Yes. They all show in the same network, each with its own hue once two or more are active (see subagents and sessions). Use the Session filter or the chips in the Sessions line to look at one at a time.
faq.several-repos.a:
Yes, one viewer per repo, each on its own port: the first takes 7777, the next 7778, and so on. Two viewers on the same repo are not allowed; the second one refuses to start.

neu lslists the running viewers with repo, port, address and process ID
neu open [repo]opens a viewer's page again. Without a repo it opens the one for the repo you are in, or the only one running
neu stop [repo]closes that viewer; --all closes every one
faq.replay.a:
Yes. Every event is saved in <repo>/.neurons/events.jsonl (paths and metadata only). To watch it again:

neu replay ~/projects/api

You can also pass a .jsonl file, or press Replay log in the live view. Replay has play, pause, restart and speeds of 1x, 2x and 5x. Silences longer than 3 seconds are cut to 3 seconds, and the page tells you how much time it skipped.
faq.timeline.a:
The third view, next to 3D and 2D. It answers when and in what order the agent touched each file. Each file becomes a row the first time Claude touches it, grouped by folder, and every action is a mark at its moment in the action's color. Your prompts appear as turns along the top, subagents get their own lane, and skills and MCP calls have a group of their own.

Scroll the wheel to zoom, drag to move, use Shift and the wheel (or the left column) to scroll the rows, and press F to follow live. Click a mark for its details, or a row for that file's history.
faq.detail.q: How do I see the details of an action?
faq.detail.a:
Click a row in the activity feed, or a mark in the Timeline. A drawer opens with the time, session, agent, tool and paths, plus whatever applies to that action: the Bash command (with written content blanked out), Claude's own description of why it ran it, the search pattern, how long it took and the first line of an error. The arrow keys move to the previous and next event, Esc closes it, and Show in graph points the camera at the file.

Click a file node to see every event for that file.

The live stream is a switch in the panel. It shows a short floating line over the network, such as "Reading src/api/orders.ts", for whatever Claude is doing right now.
faq.tools.q: What do the Tools counters show?
faq.tools.a: The Tools section of the panel counts what the agent used, in four groups: skills by name, MCP calls by server and tool, CLI programs that Bash commands ran (git, npm, gh and so on) and Claude's built-in tools such as Read, Edit or Agent.
faq.touches.q: What does it touch on my machine?
faq.touches.a:
While neu runs:

  1. It writes HTTP hooks into <repo>/.claude/settings.local.json, pointing at its own server on 127.0.0.1. Hooks you already had there stay. If the file did not exist, it creates it.
  2. It turns on bashEditDiffEnabled in ~/.claude/settings.json (or in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), so Claude Code reports which files each Bash command changed. If it was already on, it is left alone. --no-bash-diff skips this. A record of the change lives in ~/.claude/neurons/ with 0600 permissions.
  3. It creates <repo>/.neurons/ with the event log and a lock. That folder and settings.local.json go into .git/info/exclude, so they never show in git status.
  4. It notes the viewer in ~/.neurons/viewers/<pid>.json so ls, open and stop can find it.

When it closes, it removes its hooks, reverts bashEditDiffEnabled and deletes its entry. If nothing else changed in between, the files end up identical byte for byte. It never sends a signal to your Claude Code sessions, and neu stop only signals a process after ps confirms it is that viewer.
faq.crash.a:
If the viewer dies without cleaning up, its hooks stay and point at a server that is gone, so Claude Code prints a red hook error on each tool call. Fix it with:

neu uninstall ~/projects/api

That removes the hooks and reverts bashEditDiffEnabled. The next neu on that repo also fixes whatever was left. neu doctor tells you when there are hooks without a viewer. If a viewer hangs and does not close within 8 seconds, neu stop --force kills it and does the cleanup itself.
faq.content.q: Does it see what my files contain?
faq.content.a:
No. Claude Code's hook messages do include content (what a Write puts in a file, the old and new text of an Edit, the output of a command), and the server drops all of it before anything else happens. The page and the log only get paths and metadata.

Bash commands are shown so you know what ran, with heredoc bodies cut and quoted text blanked out when a command writes files or runs inline code. Command output never leaves the server; for searches, the server only takes the file paths out of the results and checks them against the tree. A failed tool keeps the first line of its error. Everything stays on 127.0.0.1.
faq.demo.q: How do I demo it without breaking anything?
faq.demo.a:
Clone Neurons itself (or any repo) into a throwaway folder, let Claude change whatever it wants there, and delete the clone at the end. Your real repos and settings stay out of it. Tested on 2026-10-03 with Claude Code 2.1.288: the network stayed at 114 nodes, the worktree subagent showed up on src/cli/ with its worktree tag, and ~/.claude/settings.json was identical after closing.

git clone ~/neurons /tmp/neurons-demo-clone
cd /tmp/neurons-demo-clone && neu      # terminal 1: opens the page
cd /tmp/neurons-demo-clone && claude   # terminal 2

Then paste this prompt into Claude Code:

This is a throwaway clone of Neurons, so you can change anything. Do this in order and answer briefly at the end:
1. Use grep to find where "bashEditDiff" is used in src/ and list the .ts files in web/src.
2. Read src/server/server.ts, src/server/attribution.ts and web/src/effects.ts.
3. In src/server/eventlog.ts add a one-line comment at the very top: "// demo: edit seen in Neurons".
4. Create docs/demo-notes.md with three lines that sum up what attribution.ts does.
5. Rename docs/PAYLOADS.md to docs/payloads-phase0.md with git mv.
6. Delete scripts/make-demo-repo.sh with rm.
7. Run "cat does-not-exist.txt" (it will fail on purpose).
8. Launch two subagents in parallel: one with the Agent tool and isolation "worktree" that reads all of src/cli/ and tells you which commands exist, and another without a worktree that reads test/unit/attribution.test.ts and tells you how many cases it tests.
9. With what they tell you, add one line at the end of docs/demo-notes.md.

To throw it away: neu stop (or Ctrl+C in terminal 1) and rm -rf /tmp/neurons-demo-clone.
faq.demo-small.q: Is there a smaller demo repo?
faq.demo-small.a:
Yes. scripts/make-demo-repo.sh creates a 14-file shop API in TypeScript, with a CLAUDE.md, a src/CLAUDE.md and a rule in .claude/rules/api.md, so you can watch instructions load on their own.

~/neurons/scripts/make-demo-repo.sh ~/neurons-demo
cd ~/neurons-demo && neu      # terminal 1
cd ~/neurons-demo && claude   # terminal 2

A prompt that walks through every kind of action:

I'm exploring this repo. Do this in order, one step at a time:
1. Find every .ts file in the project and search for TODO comments.
2. Read src/api/products.ts, src/api/orders.ts and src/utils/money.ts.
3. In src/api/products.ts, replace the TODO in getProduct with a check that throws an Error if id is empty.
4. Create src/api/health.ts with a function health() that returns { ok: true }.
5. Delete src/utils/legacy-format.ts with rm from Bash (nothing uses it).
6. Hand this task to a subagent: read src/services/cart.ts and tests/cart.test.ts and tell you whether the test covers cartTotal.
Answer briefly at the end.
StepWhat lights up
Session startCLAUDE.md glows violet; your own ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md appears in the outside cluster
1, searcha blue pulse at the root and faint flashes on the files found
2, readscyan light down to each file, faint first, then full
Inside src/apisrc/CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/api.md turn violet with no tool involved
3, editamber on products.ts
4, createa new health.ts node appears with a green flash
5, deletered on legacy-format.ts, which then leaves the tree
6, subagentits reads carry a ring of another color

To see an external change, delete a file from another terminal while the viewer runs. It shows in dim gray.
faq.how.a:
Claude Code sends each event as an HTTP hook to the neu server on 127.0.0.1. The server answers right away with an empty 204, so Claude never waits on it, then turns the event into paths relative to the repo, sends it to the page over a WebSocket and appends it to .neurons/events.jsonl. A disk watcher catches changes made outside Claude and marks them as external.

The architecture page explains it step by step with animated diagrams.
faq.os.q: Which operating systems does it run on?
faq.os.a:
SystemStatusNotes
macOSVerifiedAutomated tests and real Claude Code sessions on Apple Silicon (M4).
LinuxExpected to workThe test suite is meant to run on Linux in CI, which has not run yet. The disk watcher watches every subfolder (including node_modules and .git) and can hit the inotify limit; if it does, the viewer warns you and keeps working with Claude's events only, without external changes. Opening the browser with xdg-open is untested.
WindowsExperimentalWritten for, never run. Path matching (drive letters, case, Git Bash paths like /c/...) has not been checked against real Claude Code payloads. Windows ends a process at once, so neu stop does the cleanup itself; if that fails, run neu uninstall. Open Claude Code sessions are not detected at start. The managed settings path has not been checked.
faq.lang.q: How do I change the language?
faq.lang.a: In this guide and in the viewer, use the EN and ES buttons at the top; both remember your choice. In the terminal, add --lang en or --lang es, or set NEURONS_LANG. Without either, neu follows your system language.
faq.publish.q: Will it be on npm or Homebrew?
faq.publish.a: Not yet, and there is no date. For now you install it from the repository with npm link. The package is already set up for npm (name neurons-cli, the two commands, only dist/ is shipped), so publishing it later would make the install a single npm install -g neurons-cli. A Homebrew formula could come after that.
